8.0.s.en: (3) The manner of the Lord's speaking with Moses

8.0.0.en: The place of the lampstand was the sanctuary, and it consisted of a base and a shaft bearing seven lamps, that is, lights for illumination.

8.0.1.en: When thou lightest the lamps: that is, when you have cleaned them, filled them with oil and put them in their place on the lampstand. Over against the candlestick: the lampstand here means the middle shaft, and the meaning is that at the lighting the three right-hand lamps face toward the left and the three left-hand lamps face toward the right, so that all six lamps face toward the middle shaft.

8.0.2.en: The Lord commanded Moses that after he prepares the lampstand for lighting, Aaron is to light it, because the priests alone are permitted to light the lamps of the lampstand, since it is inside the sanctuary which only the priests enter, and the lampstand was lit from the holy fire that came down from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering. See also what was said about the lampstand and its lighting in (Ex 25:31-40).

8.1.0.en: This verse shows Aaron's complete commitment to carrying out all that God commanded.

8.2.0.en: As for the workmanship of the lampstand and the material it was made of, it was as follows:

8.2.1.en: Beaten work: that is, it was made of gold by hammering and carving, since God forbade that it be made cast (Ex 32). The specifications of the lampstand were exactly like the pattern the Lord showed Moses on the mountain (Ex 25), with its seven lamps. It was made of gold not cast but beaten, so that God might keep the people away from the memory of the cast gods that the Egyptians worshiped.

8.2.2.en: The lampstand was a symbol of Christ, "the light of the world ..." and Christ gave His children to be a light of the world also, to bear witness to His name ... Are we truly so? Grant us, O Lord, to be so for the glory of Your holy name.

8.2.3.en: (2) The ordination and consecration of the Levites (vv. 5-15:) 5 And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, 6 "Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them. 7 And thus shalt thou do unto them, to cleanse them: Sprinkle water of purifying upon them, and let them shave all their flesh, and let them wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean. 8 Then let them take a young bullock with his meat offering, even fine flour mingled with oil, and another young bullock shalt thou take for a sin offering. 9 And thou shalt bring the Levites before the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt gather the whole assembly of the children of Israel together: 10 And thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites: 11 And Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD for an offering of the children of Israel, that they may execute the service of the LORD. 12 And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the heads of the bullocks: and thou shalt offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, unto the LORD, to make an atonement for the Levites. 13 And thou shalt set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer them for an offering unto the LORD. 14 Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine. 15 And after that shall the Levites go in to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt cleanse them, and offer them for an offering." The discourse moves us, through a new divine command, to the consecration and setting apart of the Levites for service, and this included four stages:

8.2.4.en: 1- Their cleansing (vv. 5-9) 2- The laying on of hands upon them (v. 10)

8.2.5.en: 3- Their waving before the Lord (v. 11) 4- The offering of sacrifices for them (vv. 12-15)

8.3.0.en: The Lord commanded Moses to take the Levites prepared for the service from among the tribes of the children of Israel and begin to cleanse them. The bodily cleansing that Moses will perform for them also points to the purity of the spirit, and the counterpart of the Levites in the New Testament are the deacons who help the priests in the service.

8.4.0.en: The steps of the cleansing itself were as follows:

8.4.1.en: 1- Sprinkling water of purifying: that is, the water made for purification from sin. There are two opinions: either it was water from the laver from whose water the priests washed, or it was other water mixed with the ashes of a sin offering, as was done in the law of the water of separation (ch. 19). The Levites were sprinkled with it; and this rite points to cleansing from sin.

8.4.2.en: 2- Letting a razor pass over their flesh: this is the second step, which means shaving all the hair of their skin with the razor, as a reference to removing sin from all its roots.

8.4.3.en: 3- Washing the clothes: also as a reference that a person's outward conduct, which the clothes point to, must be in keeping with inner purity, so that a person behaves with purity and righteousness toward all those around him.

8.5.0.en: The Levites, of course, had to prepare the sacrifices that they would offer at their consecration, and they were two bullocks offered as a sacrifice, one of them a burnt offering of delight to the Lord, and the other a sin offering, with an offering of flour mingled with oil.

8.5.1.en: The spiritual meaning in this is that when a person comes forward to the service of the Lord he must come first with repentance, that is, with a sin offering, and offer his whole life for the delight of God's heart as a burnt offering. All the men of God and His holy servants throughout the ages of the Church were daily sacrifices poured out on the altar of service.

8.6.0.en: The discourse here is to Moses the prophet, that he bring all the Levites before the door of the Tent and the people gather around them for the beginning of the celebrations and rites of consecration.

8.7.0.en: Before the Lord: before the door of the tent of meeting.

8.7.1.en: Because the Levites are chosen basically from the people, the children of Israel lay their hands on them as a sign that they are the sacrifices offered by the people to God and to the service. The laying on of hands also carries the meaning of calling and consecration for the one on whom the hand is laid, and likewise the people's declaration that they are their deputies for the service of God. Of course the whole people would not lay hands on the Levites, but only the elders and the heads of the people.

8.8.0.en: The sacrifices or offerings were "waved" before the Lord, that is, some pieces of them were taken and the priest moved them with his hands in all directions and raised and lowered them as a sign that this sacrifice belongs to the Lord and is presented to Him. The waving of the Levites has the same spiritual meaning: Aaron, and whoever succeeds him in the headship of the priesthood, comes and gently moves the Levites to declare that they belong to the Lord and are living sacrifices presented to Him on behalf of all the people of the children of Israel, so that by this rite the Levite becomes a servant of the Lord.

8.9.0.en: Then the sacrifices are offered by the usual rite, both the burnt offering and the sin offering, with the Levite laying his hand on the head of the sacrifice before it is slain (see Lev 1, 2). Just as the people appointed the Levites in their place for the service and as a redemption of the firstborn of the people, so the sacrifices redeem the Levites by their blood before God, as a clear sign and symbol of Christ's redemption by His blood of all His people. He is the true living sacrifice who was offered once on the Cross and has been extended to us with every Divine Liturgy until His second coming.

8.10.0.en: This verse came as a repetition of what came in (v. 11), and the purpose is not to repeat the waving after the sacrifices but to stress the spiritual meaning, that they were fully set apart for the service of God. We notice also that God will repeat this command a third time in (v. 15).

8.11.0.en: Thou shalt separate: that is, set apart and bring out.

8.11.1.en: The inspired text affirms what is known and practiced, that the Levites are separated from the people and set apart for the service only, and God declares clearly His ownership of them: "the Levites shall be mine." Thus, after the rite of ordination and setting apart, the work of the Levites becomes the service of the tent of meeting according to all that has been explained, and the last words of the inspired text in this section are an affirmation of the necessity of inner and outer purity and the declaration of ownership belonging to God alone.

8.11.2.en: Care for the consecration of your heart to God by driving out evil thoughts through repeating the Psalms and prayers, and keep your goal clear before your eyes always, which is the love of God.

8.12.s.en: (3) The Levites instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel

8.12.0.en: Although it is God who chose and set apart the Levites for His service, He also regards them as a gift and present from the people to Him, giving His people the honor of presenting the tribe of their brother Levi to Him and to His service. Besides this being humility from God and great fatherly love, it also teaches us that when a father and mother accept God's choice of one of their sons as a priest or a monk, God regards this acceptance as a gift that He receives and values very highly from the father and mother.

8.13.0.en: God again reminds the people that His choice of the Levites was a substitute and redemption for offering every firstborn of the people, and this takes us back to the events of the tenth plague when God smote the firstborn of the Egyptians and put them to death, and in return He sanctified, that is, set apart for Himself, all the firstborn of the children of Israel, and silver was offered for them to the Lord ... But after the crossing of the Red Sea, and the people's need of the Tent for servants to serve God and His dwelling, God substituted the Levites for the firstborn of the people.

8.14.0.en: After God set the Levites apart for Himself instead of the firstborn, He put them under the authority of the priests, that is, Aaron and his sons, and their task is as follows:

8.14.1.en: 1- Serving the house of the Lord, that is, the Tent, under the supervision of the priests, taking it down when journeying and setting it up when settling.

8.14.2.en: 2- Making atonement for the children of Israel: the Levites had to alert the people and warn them against transgressing the commandments or touching or defiling the Tent and its appurtenances. By this they averted the wrath of God against His people, so that no plague would strike them when they draw near to God in worship or in offering sacrifices.

8.15.0.en: Aaron made an atonement for them to cleanse them: he offered sacrifices for them.

8.15.1.en: These three verses come as a summary of all that the Lord commanded Moses concerning the sanctification and cleansing of the Levites, the offering of sacrifices for them and their waving before the Lord to begin their service; and the words "Moses did, thus did the children of Israel unto them, so did they unto them" are mentioned to stress that everything God commanded was carried out with all precision.

8.15.2.en: Moses was exact in fulfilling all that the Lord commanded with all faithfulness; may we, beloved, learn to be faithful to the rites of the Church and to learn them, for whoever preserves the rite and order of the Church preserves the Church herself.

8.16.s.en: (4) The age of the Levites' service

8.16.0.en: God defined for Moses the age at which the Levites begin the service of the Lord, which is from the age of twenty-five, although at the beginning of the fourth chapter He set the age of the Levites who perform the service at thirty. From this it is understood that the Levites actually began from the age of twenty-five as assistant servants and as a period of preparation and training for them, so as to carry the full responsibilities at the age of thirty.

8.17.0.en: From the age of thirty to fifty the Levites perform the full and arduous service, but after the age of fifty, with the beginning of the weakness of their bodies, they perform a light service and leave the carrying of what is difficult, and are content with guarding, direction and guidance.

8.17.1.en: Whatever your age, you have a role in the Church, so offer what you can, and let no one despise your youth, and do not be lazy because of your old age, for your service, however small it may seem, has great value in the eyes of God, especially if it is out of your need, that is, if you offer to God whatever your weakness.

8.17.2.en: The reminder of the keeping of the Passover and the pillar of cloud and fire

9.0.s.en: (1) Keeping the Passover at its appointed time

9.0.0.en: The Lord spoke to Moses: the speech of God to Moses here does not follow the order of the events of the previous chapters, for the time here is clear and specific, the first month of the second year of the Exodus, whereas the numbering and counting of the people was in the second month of the same year; that is, God's speaking with Moses in this chapter about keeping the Passover preceded what came in the first chapter about the numbering of the people.

9.1.0.en: Because of the importance of the Passover sacrifice, which redeemed the firstborn of the people and is a type of Christ's redemption of us, God required the people to keep it at its appointed time and without postponement. Its date was set in (Ex 12) as the evening of the fourteenth day of Nisan, which is the first month of the religious year and the seventh in the civil year. The words "in its appointed season" include not only the day but the time of eating it, which is between the two evenings, which now corresponds in the time known to us to between the afternoon and before sunset.

9.2.0.en: According to all the rites of it shall ye keep it: that is, according to all that God explained before of slaying, cleaning, roasting and eating, which are the ordinances that the people kept well and which were explained before in (Ex 12), and are also referred to in (Lev 23).

9.3.0.en: As the Lord spoke to Moses and commanded him, so the people did and obeyed with all exactness, and they ate the Passover between the two evenings exactly as its ordinances prescribe.

9.3.1.en: The children of Israel kept the first Passover in Egypt, and this is the second Passover, at the beginning of the second year of their departure from Egypt, and unfortunately they were afterward occupied with their sins and murmurings, so they did not keep the Passover until after they entered the Promised Land under Joshua. In the New Testament, however, the Church is careful to celebrate the sacrament of Communion of the Body and Blood of the Lord, of which the Passover was a type, because this sacrament is the food and strength of Christians.

9.3.2.en: Christ our Passover is present on the altar every day, and the times of the prayers are known to all, so are you careful to attend the Divine Liturgy early, and do you teach your children such care? My brother, a small word in your ear: "care means respect," so what do laziness, laxity and lateness mean?!

9.4.s.en: (2) Rulings concerning one who refrained from eating the Passover

9.4.0.en: A case appeared here that needed guidance and clarification from Moses the prophet and Aaron his brother the priest. This exceptional case was that when the children of Israel kept the Passover at its appointed time, a relative of some of the people died, and they were defiled by touching him and burying him, and according to the provisions of the Law they could not approach the Passover or practice its rites. This pained them, the feeling that they would be separated from the people and miss this grace, which is the eating of the Passover that is kept only once a year, so they came forward to Moses and Aaron and asked them, sorrowful at their being separated.

9.5.0.en: But Moses the faithful servant did not come with an opinion of his own, but asked them to wait until he heard the opinion and command of the Lord on this matter, and he entered the Tent and God spoke with him as usual from above the ark of the testimony and from between the cherubim.

9.5.1.en: If only you would learn, when you answer a person who asked you for guidance or advice, to lift your heart toward God, asking Him for opinion and help before you answer his question.

9.6.0.en: The Lord's answer to those who asked was comforting and reassuring, and the Lord made His answer a law binding on all generations: whoever was defiled by a dead person, or whose circumstances of travel to a distant place prevented him from keeping the law of the Passover at its appointed time, must keep the Passover on the same day, that is, the fourteenth of the following month, which is the second of the religious year, and must observe in keeping it all that came in the Law: eating it between the two evenings, and eating it with unleavened bread and not with leavened bread, and also with bitter herbs, and leaving none of it until the morning ... see all that was said about the Passover in (Ex 12). We see from this God's mercy and flexibility in carrying out His commandments, for He seeks an excuse for those in special circumstances. This responsibility is carried out in the Church of the New Testament by the father of confession in guiding those in special circumstances.

9.7.0.en: But whoever was lax without any of the previous excuses that God mentioned, and did not take part in keeping and eating the Passover, that person will bear the result of his neglect and carelessness and is thereby exposed to the punishment of God, while the congregation of the people must cut him off and separate him, that is, put him away from itself, so that he is not of it any longer.

9.8.0.en: The stranger: the incomer who became a Jew, that is, not of the offspring of the tribes but who joined the people and was circumcised.

9.8.1.en: Born in the land: that is, a Hebrew Jew of the offspring of Abraham and Isaac.

9.8.2.en: God allowed every person who joined the people to share in the Passover offering with all its laws, even if he was a stranger who had joined, but he must first be circumcised ... for God in His love receives all, but faith and circumcision are required, as we say now that faith and Baptism are required.

9.8.3.en: Make allowance for those around you and do not be harsh in your judgments of them, and encourage them to live with God and to correct their errors, so that they come to love the spiritual life and love you.

9.9.s.en: (3) The pillar of cloud and fire, and the journeying

9.9.0.en: The day that the tabernacle was reared up: when the tent of meeting was set up for the first time. The names are used interchangeably for the same thing: the tent of meeting is the tent of the testimony, and it is the tabernacle.

9.9.1.en: As one of the signs of God's love for His people and His tender care, the cloud, that is, the pillar of cloud, accompanied the people from their departure from Egypt until they reached the Promised Land. It guided them and shaded them, keeping the scorching sun from them, and when night came the pillar of cloud turned into a pillar of fire to give them light and guide them also.

9.9.2.en: On the day the Tent was first set up, God descended upon the Tent with His glory and blessing, and the cloud thickened and grew until it covered the whole Tent, and likewise at night the sight was awesome, for the pillar of fire enwrapped the Tent and went up from it and above it in the form of great glory (Ex 40). The pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire declare the presence of God in the midst of His people and His care for them, and they are a symbol of the mystery of the Incarnation and the union of divinity with humanity: the fire and the cloud signify divinity, and the material Tent signifies humanity.

9.10.1.en: God alone determined when the people would depart and when they would encamp, because He is their leader: "at the commandment of the Lord." The sign for that was the lifting of the cloud or its descending. If the cloud was lifted, the Levites began to take down the Tent for the journey and all the people followed them, and if the cloud abode again, the people also followed it and pitched their tents around the house of the Lord.

9.11.0.en: These five verses came as a confirmation and detailing of what was mentioned before in (vv. 19, 20), affirming in sum that whether the days were few or many, there was no journeying and no encamping except at the command of the Lord ... And in verses (21-23) it affirms again that even if the cloud was lifted for one day and then came down, the journeying would be for one day and the encamping for one day, and in all cases it was God who set the timetable and the people obeyed Him.

9.11.1.en: They kept the charge of the Lord: that is, as soon as they encamped they began to set up the Tent and begin worship at once, to complete the rites and offer the sacrifices as God had spoken before and made clear to Moses.

9.11.2.en: May we learn to commit all the affairs of our life to God, and leave to Him the ordering and the leading, and receive the blessing of obedience ... For all of man's problems begin when his will is separated from the will of God ... Be careful to pray and ask for God's good counsel before you begin any work.

9.11.3.en: The two silver trumpets and the people's departure from Sinai
